text:
Tony DeAngelo has eight points in 22 games on an Islanders team that keeps winning, and our numbers think he has been unlucky. New York has scored about 5.4 fewer goals than its chances with him on the ice, which has cost him points, and that usually swings back. He had a goal and an assist in the 5-1 win over Columbus last week, and he and Matthew Schaefer earned the postgame honors that night.

The concern with DeAngelo has always been the other end, and it still is. Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more with him on last season than against all but 1% of defensemen. This season the Islanders are about even at five on five with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances). The offense is real: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him in the 91st percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists. He is paired with Adam Pelech at morning skate. Our range has him around 35 points. As always with him, the partner matters.
